examples.gloss: If it is cheap, I will buy it.
If you hurry, you will make it.
If you read it, you will understand.

usage: A conditional that treats the first clause as the one requirement for the second: 安ければ買う, 'if it is cheap, I will buy'.
い-adjectives use ければ. Nouns and な-adjectives use なら.
After an action, a request or command in the second clause often sounds odd. Use たら there.
Also in fixed phrases: よければ, できれば, 見れば分かる.

compare.difference: たら is the all-purpose 'if' or 'when' and works with requests and past events. ば is narrower.
と describes results that follow automatically. ば sets a requirement.
